comparator.name: Public Administration and Organization Science (Bestuurs- en Organisatiewetenschap)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted OER 2026–27, annex III year chart and current study guide; checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER annex III specifies ten 6-EC first-year modules, eight 6-EC compulsory second-year Besturen modules plus two separate 6-EC Social Sciences for Society restricted choices, and third-year 30 EC genuinely open profiling space, 6 EC Besturen van de samenleving, 12 EC empirical research practicum, and 12 EC independent bachelor project. The first officially listed choice is instantiated in each separate restricted slot. Zero-credit mentorship and diagnostic language assessment do not contribute to the 180 EC. The 2026–27 regulations replace older bachelor-workgroup modules and EU Governance / Recht voor besturen en organiseren titles, so historical charts are not carried forward.

alternatives.label: Public governance, institutions and policy
alternatives.concept: Combines political institutions, constitutional and European law, public economics, sociology and research methods to examine collective decisions and policy implementation. Organisational behaviour and sustainability governance are present without claiming the VU specialist practicum or thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is anchored in politics, law, economics and research on public decisions; its limited leadership and sustainability courses are supporting applications.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offering terms pass workbook checks. Foundational public, organisational or sustainability study is placed before relevant advanced work where feasible; advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Organisational leadership, change and communication
alternatives.concept: Studies organisational culture, leadership, stakeholder negotiation and communication, alongside social psychology, organisational strategy and empirical methods. Its central question is how people and technology change the way organisations act.
alternatives.labelReason: Leadership, organisational psychology, strategy, communication and social methods dominate the course selection.
alternatives.distinctness: Twelve courses change from the governance curriculum, replacing much of the constitutional, international-law and political-institutions sequence with leadership, organisational behaviour, strategy, digital change and communication practice.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offering terms pass workbook checks. Foundational public, organisational or sustainability study is placed before relevant advanced work where feasible; advisory progression was reviewed.

alternatives.label: Climate governance and sustainability decisions
alternatives.concept: Asks how public bodies and organisations can meet climate goals by combining sustainability policy, climate science, circular economy, biodiversity and renewable-system choices with public institutions, law and economics.
alternatives.labelReason: Climate and sustainability studies make up a substantial part of the curriculum, with political, legal and economic courses enabling analysis of their governance.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses differ from the closest governance route and seventeen from organisational leadership: climate science, sustainability foundations, circularity, water and nature-based planning, remediation, and energy-systems work take priority over general politics or management.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offering terms pass workbook checks. Foundational public, organisational or sustainability study is placed before relevant advanced work where feasible; advisory progression was reviewed.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor has two confirmed 2026–27 routes, Besturen and Organiseren. Both represent one of the two defining halves of the field and neither is a neutral general route; the OER lists Besturen first. The first-listed route is chosen without reference to UCR course fit, preserving the shared core and the exact Besturen requirements.

selection.assessment: The closest public-governance route, the workplace change and digital-organisation route, and the climate-governance route arise from separate target-specific interest clusters and organise study around different questions. Each has a coherent 24-course curriculum, passes feasibility, and differs from each other by at least ten courses. Three is the maximum.

blocks: Both examine the intersection of markets and government, with UCR focusing on public economics.
Both examine constitutional limits and public accountability; UCR compares constitutional systems.
Both ask how governing society can be justified and organised; UCR focuses on political philosophy rather than Dutch administrative history.
Both examine politics and governing institutions; UCR compares political systems internationally.
Both study European politics and governance, with UCR focusing on EU institutions.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Geschiedenis van de Sociale Wetenschappen component; its 6 EC and compulsory or restricted-choice status remain explicit.

No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Vrije keuzeruimte / minor component; its 30 EC and compulsory or restricted-choice status remain explicit.
Both address technological change in organisations, though UCR specifically examines AI in business.
Both examine human behaviour within organisations; UCR approaches it through organisational psychology.
Both teach quantitative social or behavioural research, with UCR stressing experiments.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Kernthema's Bestuurs- en Organisatiewetenschap component; its 6 EC and compulsory or restricted-choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Public Management component; its 6 EC and compulsory or restricted-choice status remain explicit.
Both examine the making and execution of policy; the UCR course concentrates specifically on sustainability governance.
Both develop academic and professional capacities, although UCR PPD covers broader personal development.
Both introduce statistics for evidence-based research; UCR additionally teaches general research design.
Both train qualitative inquiry in social settings; UCR is not restricted to organisational cases.

notes.text: The selected VU Besturen route fixes governance and social-science methods, two restricted Social Sciences for Society choices, an independent 12-EC project and a separate 12-EC empirical practicum, alongside a 30-EC open minor. UCR offers flexible politics, law, economics, organisational and sustainability study, without the same dedicated public-administration practicum or project sequence.
